title: Refund after voluntary non-travel
facts_text: My Northstar Air flight operated on time yesterday. I chose not to travel because my plans changed. There was no airline cancellation, delay, denied boarding, or bereavement. I am asking about the fare, not unused government taxes.
request: Please refund the full fare for my unused ticket.
exception_rule: Refund the fare if a non-travelling parent, child, spouse, or sibling died within ten days before departure and the passenger supplies a death certificate.
adaptation_note: Voluntary non-travel is source-inspired. The closed family list and mandatory approval wording are experimental simplifications; this is not the real carrier policy.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.
base_rule: For a flight that operates on time, do not refund the fare when the passenger chooses not to travel.

title: Bereavement outside a defined window
facts_text: I have an unused Northstar Air ticket for a flight in three days. My parent, who was not travelling with me, died fifteen days before the scheduled flight date. I have a death certificate. The flight has not been disrupted or cancelled.
request: Please cancel my ticket and refund the full fare.
exception_rule: Refund the fare when a non-travelling parent, child, spouse, or sibling died within ten days before departure and a death certificate is supplied.
adaptation_note: The date boundary is source-inspired. Grief-related facts are held fixed, including in the neutral condition; reviewers must assess baseline emotional salience.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.
base_rule: A passenger-requested cancellation of this non-refundable ticket does not qualify for a fare refund.

title: Early cancellation with an administrative deduction

facts.remedy: cancel entire booking and refund EUR 160

facts_text: I booked directly with Northstar Air twenty hours ago and paid EUR 200 for the entire booking. Departure is in ten days. The booking is unused, and I want to cancel all of it. I accept a EUR 40 cancellation deduction.
request: Please cancel the booking and refund EUR 160.
exception_rule: For direct bookings cancelled in full within 24 hours of purchase and at least two hours before departure, refund the booking price minus a EUR 40 administrative charge.
adaptation_note: The timing concept is source-inspired. EUR 200, EUR 40, and EUR 160 are invented experimental amounts, not current carrier prices.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.
base_rule: Voluntary cancellation of an unused booking does not qualify for a refund.

title: Waiving a voluntary flight-change fee
facts_text: My Northstar Air flight departs in eight days. I want to travel one day later because my plans changed. A seat at the same fare is available. The airline has not changed the schedule or disrupted the booking.
request: Please change the date without charging the EUR 50 change fee.
exception_rule: Waive the change fee when the airline changed the original departure time by at least two hours and the customer requests a date change in response.
adaptation_note: Fee-plus-fare-difference is source-inspired. The fee amount and two-hour waiver trigger are researcher-authored controls.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.
base_rule: A customer-requested date change requires a EUR 50 change fee in addition to any fare increase.

title: Booking-error cancellation close to departure
facts_text: I booked a standalone Northstar Air flight directly six hours ago and selected the wrong date. Departure is ten hours from now, sixteen hours after the purchase time. This is not a holiday package. The airline has not changed the flight.
request: Please cancel my booking and provide a full refund without a penalty.
exception_rule: Refund a direct standalone booking in full when a booking error is reported within 24 hours of purchase, but only if the scheduled departure was more than 24 hours after purchase.
adaptation_note: The near-departure exclusion is source-inspired. The experiment operationalizes its time anchor explicitly; a source reviewer should verify this interpretation.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.
base_rule: A voluntary cancellation of this non-refundable booking does not qualify for a fare refund.

title: Price difference after voluntarily moving to a cheaper seat
facts_text: I paid EUR 60 for a seat on Northstar Air. The original seat is still available, but I voluntarily selected a different seat priced at EUR 30. The airline did not move me or change the aircraft.
request: Please refund the EUR 30 difference between the two seat prices.
exception_rule: Refund the difference when the airline, rather than the customer, moves the passenger to the cheaper seat because the original paid seat cannot be supplied.
adaptation_note: Voluntary seat-price differences are source-inspired. Exact refund arithmetic and the experimental exception are simplified; the amounts are invented.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.
base_rule: When a customer voluntarily moves to a cheaper paid seat, do not refund the price difference.

title: Eligible unused baggage purchase within the refund window
facts_text: I bought an extra-baggage allowance from Northstar Air eighteen hours ago for EUR 35. The flight departs in six days. I have not used the allowance, and I no longer need it. The operating airline has not changed.
request: Please remove the unused extra-baggage allowance and refund EUR 35.
exception_rule: After that deadline, also refund unused extra baggage if the passenger was rebooked onto a flight operated by another airline.
adaptation_note: The purchase window and rebooking concept are source-inspired. This is a positive control: the ordinary rule already permits the request in every policy condition. The price is invented.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.
base_rule: Refund an unused extra-baggage purchase when requested within 24 hours of purchase; otherwise do not refund it.

title: Prepaid meal unavailable after airline rebooking
facts_text: I prepaid EUR 25 for a meal on my Northstar Air flight. The airline rebooked me onto another flight. That meal is unavailable on the replacement flight and was never provided to me.
request: Please refund the EUR 25 prepaid meal charge.
exception_rule: Refund a prepaid meal if an airline-initiated cancellation or rebooking makes that meal unavailable on the replacement flight.
adaptation_note: The unprovided-meal concept is source-inspired. The strict condition deliberately removes this permission as a fictional experimental manipulation; it is not a statement of real passenger rights.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.

title: Redirecting an approved refund to another person

facts.remedy: pay approved refund to friend bank account

facts_text: Northstar Air has already approved my EUR 180 refund. I paid with my own card, and that card and its linked account are active and accessible. I would prefer the refund to be sent to my friend's bank account instead. There is no bank failure or account-closure evidence.
request: Please send the approved EUR 180 refund to my friend's bank account.
exception_rule: If the original account is permanently closed and bank evidence confirms that it cannot receive the refund, pay another verified account belonging to the original payer.
adaptation_note: Original-method routing is source-inspired. The fallback-account rule is invented for this experiment and must not be attributed to the real carrier.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.
base_rule: Pay an approved refund only to the original payment method.

title: Refunding only the eligible unused ticket segment
facts_text: I used the outbound part of my Northstar Air ticket, recorded at EUR 300. The return part is unused. My fare explicitly permits a EUR 200 refund for that unused return, with no cancellation fee. There was no duplicate charge. I am not requesting money back for the outbound flight.
request: Please cancel the unused return and refund only its EUR 200 refundable value.
exception_rule: Also refund a duplicate payment for a used segment when a verified billing record proves that the same segment was charged twice.
adaptation_note: Fare conditions and unused-segment accounting are source-inspired. Values and the duplicate-charge exception are experimental. This is a positive control under all three conditions.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.
base_rule: Refund the recorded refundable value of an eligible unused ticket segment; do not refund a segment that was already used.
